lp_tagline: Bring a malware dataset, train and compare machine-learning models with a leakage-free pipeline, see which features drive their decisions, and classify new samples. All in one place.
lp_p1_d: Bring any CSV malware dataset, not only the built-in examples. You choose the label column and the features.
lp_p2_d: Every model goes through the same leakage-free pipeline, with hold-out and cross-validation, and a warning when a feature looks too good to be true.
lp_p3_d: See which features a model relies on and why it decided what it did, in charts and plain language.
lp_how_sub: Follow the steps in order. Each step opens the page where you do it.
lp_step_prep_d: Read the dataset requirements and, if you need a starting point, download the template (Datasets, Add dataset).
lp_step_add_d: Upload the CSV, choose the label column and say which values mean Benign. The tool cleans the data and registers it.
lp_step_check_d: Look at class balance, missing values, duplicates and the features that best separate the classes.
lp_step_run_d: Choose features, label mode, models and evaluation, then train. Every run is saved.
lp_step_compare_d: Open saved runs, see accuracy, F1 and confusion matrices, and compare experiments such as with or without a suspicious column.
lp_step_cross_d: Train on one dataset and test on another to check whether a model generalises.
lp_step_explain_d: See which features a model relies on, and why it decided what it did for a single sample.
lp_step_predict_d: Apply a saved model to a new CSV and download the predictions.
lp_step_sus_d: Answer the 10-question SUS usability questionnaire. No account needed.
lp_feat_sub: Pick a feature to read what it is for, what you do there, and what you get.
lp_datasets_what: The place where every analysis starts. You register the malware datasets you want to work with, check their quality and explore their features.
lp_datasets_do:
- Download the template and read the requirements.
- Upload a CSV (or add a built-in example).
- Pick the label column and say which values mean Benign.
- Choose which numeric columns are features.
- Inspect class balance, missing values, duplicates and the features that best separate the classes.
lp_datasets_get:
- A cleaned dataset saved in your workspace.
- Quality indicators and charts for every feature.
- Clear messages when a file cannot be used, and why.
lp_datasets_note: Cleaning is automatic: rows with missing or infinite values, and constant columns, are removed. Read Datasets, Add dataset, Requirements first.
lp_pipeline_what: Trains and evaluates several machine-learning models on one dataset with the same leakage-free steps: log1p, RobustScaler, SMOTE (training data only), model, evaluation.
lp_pipeline_do:
- Choose a dataset, the feature set (all, exclude some columns, or only columns shared with another dataset) and the label mode (original classes or Benign vs Malware).
- Select models (up to 10) and the evaluation: hold-out 80:20, stratified k-fold cross-validation, or both.
- Turn SMOTE on or off, choose Fast or Full model size, then run.
lp_pipeline_get:
- Accuracy, precision, recall and F1 for each model, and per fold.
- Every run is saved, so results survive a refresh.
- A warning when one feature separates the classes suspiciously well.
lp_pipeline_note: Fast uses smaller models for quick trials; Full uses larger settings for final results. Change one thing per run so the runs can be compared.
lp_models_what: Reads every saved run so you can inspect one in depth or compare several.
lp_models_do:
- Pick a run to see tables, charts and confusion matrices.
- Open Compare runs and select two or more runs, for example with and without a suspicious column.
- Download the tables as CSV.
lp_models_get:
- Which model is best, and by how much.
- Which classes each model confuses.
- The effect of a single change (features, SMOTE, label mode) on every model.
lp_models_note: Differences smaller than the standard deviation across folds are not meaningful. Compare runs on the same dataset and label mode only.
lp_cross_what: Tests whether a detector trained on one dataset still works on another dataset it has never seen.
lp_cross_do:
- Choose the training dataset and the test dataset.
- The tool uses only the columns whose names exist in both.
- Pick models and run; labels are simplified to Benign vs Malware.
lp_cross_get:
- The score inside dataset A, the score on dataset B and the drop between them.
- A short plain-language reading and a confusion matrix on the test dataset.
lp_cross_note: If the two datasets share no column names, the test cannot run. Give equivalent columns the same name in your CSV first.
lp_explain_what: Shows which features a model relies on, and why it decided what it did for a single sample.
lp_explain_do:
- Pick a run and a model.
- Read the importance chart and the plain-language summary.
- Pick a test sample (or only the mistakes) to see which features pushed the decision.
- Optionally copy a ready-made prompt to ask an AI assistant.
lp_explain_get:
- A feature ranking that works for every model (permutation importance).
- A warning when one feature dominates, which may mean leakage.
- A per-sample explanation: green bars support the decision, red bars oppose it.
lp_explain_note: Importance shows what the model uses, not what causes malware. Correlated features can share the credit.
lp_predict_what: Applies a saved model to a new CSV file and labels every row.
lp_predict_do:
- Pick a run and a model.
- Upload a CSV. Columns are matched to the model's features by name; match the rest by hand.
- Press Predict and download the results.
lp_predict_get:
- The predicted class and the confidence for every row, with a summary per class.
- Coverage figures that show how well your file fits the model.
- Accuracy on your file if it already has labels.
lp_predict_note: If fewer than half of the model's features are found, the prediction is refused. Missing features are filled with 0.
lp_sus_what: A standard 10-statement usability questionnaire (System Usability Scale) to rate this tool.
lp_sus_do:
- Answer ten statements from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree).
- Submit. No account or dataset is needed.
lp_sus_get:
- A score from 0 to 100 for each respondent, and the overall mean compared with the benchmark of 68.
- A CSV of all responses for your report.
lp_sus_note: Ask real users, not only yourself; a mean from a handful of respondents is only a rough indication.
pl_step_log1p: Compresses very large counts with log(1 + |x|) so a few huge values do not dominate.
pl_step_scaler: Rescales each feature with the median and interquartile range, so outliers have little influence. Learned on training data only.
pl_step_smote: Creates synthetic samples of the smaller classes to balance the training data. Never applied to the test data.
pl_step_model: One of up to 10 classifiers: LightGBM, XGBoost, Random Forest, Extra Trees, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, Linear SVM, KNN, Naive Bayes, MLP.
pl_step_eval: Hold-out 80:20 and/or stratified k-fold cross-validation, with accuracy, precision, recall and F1.
lp_fastfull_d: Fast uses smaller models (for example 150 to 200 trees) so you get results in seconds or minutes, which suits demos and trials. Full uses larger settings (for example 700 to 1000 trees and a lower learning rate) meant for final results. The exact settings are listed in Pipeline Runner, Model settings for Fast and Full.
lp_good:
- This is a research and learning tool, not a replacement for antivirus software.
- High accuracy depends on the dataset. A model that is excellent on one dataset may do poorly on another; Cross-Dataset tests this.
- Datasets, runs and models are stored in the storage/ folder of the computer that runs the app.
- The first run on a large dataset can take a while; start with Fast and a limited number of rows.
lp_faq_install_q: Do I need to install anything to use it?
lp_faq_install_a: No, if the app is already running you only need a browser. To run it yourself you need Python and the packages in requirements.txt.
lp_faq_format_q: What kind of data can I upload?
lp_faq_format_a: A CSV file with numeric feature columns and one label column. See Datasets, Add dataset, Requirements for the full rules and a template.
lp_faq_toogood_a: Often one feature is derived from the label (for example an antivirus detection ratio). Check the warning in Pipeline Runner and Explainability, then run again without that column and compare.
lp_faq_which_a: Run several and compare them in Model Comparison. If the differences are smaller than the standard deviation across folds, the models are practically equal.
lp_faq_av_a: No. It evaluates machine-learning models on datasets you provide. It does not scan APK files.
lp_faq_store_a: In the storage/ folder next to the app, on the computer that runs it. Everyone who uses the same running app sees the same data.
gl_perm_d: Shuffles one feature at a time and measures how much the model gets worse; a big drop means the model depends on that feature.
gl_f1m_d: The average F1 over all classes, so small classes count as much as large ones.
gd_title: Before you upload: template and requirements
gd_sub: Download a ready-made template, check what a dataset file must contain, and see what makes an upload fail.
gd_tpl_intro: A dataset is a CSV table: **one row per app sample**, **numeric feature columns**, and **one label column** that says whether the sample is Benign or malware. The table below shows the standard layout. Download it and replace the example values with your own.
gd_meaning_id: Any text that names the sample (package name, hash). It is not numeric, so it is ignored automatically.
gd_meaning_feature: A numeric measurement or count used by the models.
gd_meaning_label: The class of each row, for example Benign or Malware (or a malware family).
tp_grp_permission: Whether (1) or how often the app declares this permission.
tp_grp_api: How many times the app calls this API.
tp_grp_syscall: How many times this system call is observed at run time.
tp_grp_network: Network activity measured at run time (bytes sent).
gd_tpl_caption: Preview of the first 10 rows. The full sample has {r} rows and {c} columns.
gd_tpl_synthetic: The sample values are synthetic and only illustrate the format; they are not real malware data. The sample itself is valid, so you can upload it to try the whole workflow.
gd_api_title: Get a standard sample from an online dataset (API, optional)
gd_api_help: Fetches the first rows of a public dataset from the Hugging Face Datasets Server API, so you can see how a standard Android malware dataset is laid out. Enter a dataset id in the form owner/name. It needs an internet connection and only fetches the first rows.
tp_err_id: Enter a dataset id in the form owner/name.
tp_err_net: Could not reach the online service. Check your internet connection.
tp_err_http: The service answered with an error (HTTP {code}). The dataset may not exist, may be private, or may not support preview.
tp_err_big: The response is too large to load.
tp_err_json: The service returned an unexpected response.
tp_err_nosplit: This dataset has no previewable data.
tp_err_norows: No rows were returned for this dataset.
gd_must:
- A **CSV file** (comma or semicolon separated; UTF-8 or Latin-1 text). Excel files must be saved as CSV first.
- A **header row** with a unique name for every column.
- **One row per sample** (one app, one record).
- **One label column** with at least two different values and no more than 50.
- At least one value that means **Benign** and at least one **malware** value.
- **Numeric feature columns**: counts, 0/1 flags or measurements. A column counts as numeric when at least 90% of its values are numbers.
gd_auto:
- Rows with a missing label, or a missing or infinite feature value, are removed.
- Duplicate rows are removed (you can switch this off).
- Columns that are not numeric (names, hashes, dates) are ignored.
- Columns with the same value in every row are removed.
- A single malware value is named **Malware**; with several, the original names become the classes.
- Negative numbers are converted to their absolute value before the log1p step, so the sign is not kept.
gd_tips:
- Use at least **10 samples per class**, preferably hundreds. Cross-validation needs at least as many samples in the smallest class as the number of folds.
- Keep column names identical across datasets if you want to use Cross-Dataset.
- Avoid columns derived from the label (for example an antivirus detection ratio) unless you want to study them; the Pipeline Runner can exclude them.
- Convert text features first (for example a permission list written as one string) into one numeric 0/1 column per item.
gd_lim4_v: Up to 200 MB by default (Streamlit setting)
gd_err_intro: These are the messages you may see while adding a dataset, why they appear, and how to fix them.
gd_e_ad_err_read: The file is not a readable CSV, or its text encoding is not recognised.
gd_f_ad_err_read: Save the file again as CSV (UTF-8) from Excel or another tool.
gd_e_ad_err_label: The chosen label column has only one value, so there is nothing to classify.
gd_f_ad_err_label: Choose the column that holds the class (for example Benign or Malware), or add samples of the other class.
gd_e_ad_err_label_many: The label column has too many distinct values; it looks like an ID or a continuous number, not a class.
gd_f_ad_err_label_many: Pick the correct label column, or group the values into classes first.
gd_e_ad_err_benign: No value was marked as Benign, or every value was marked as Benign.
gd_f_ad_err_benign: Select the value(s) meaning Benign and leave at least one malware value unselected.
gd_e_ad_err_feats: No numeric feature column is left after ignoring text columns and excluded columns.
gd_f_ad_err_feats: Make sure the features are numbers, or un-exclude some columns.
gd_e_ad_err_empty: Every row was removed during cleaning, usually because each row has a missing or invalid value.
gd_f_ad_err_empty: Fill or remove the missing values in your file, and check that number columns do not contain text such as N/A.
gd_e_ad_err_name: A dataset with this name is already registered.
gd_f_ad_err_name: Use another name, or delete the old dataset.
gd_f_ad_err_noname: Type a name for the dataset.
gd_e_pl_err_small: Shown in Pipeline Runner: the smallest class has fewer samples than the number of cross-validation folds needs.
gd_f_pl_err_small: Use fewer folds or more rows, or add samples to the small class.
gd_e_ad_warn_dropped: Warning: some columns are text, so they cannot be used as features.
gd_f_ad_warn_dropped: Nothing, unless one of them should be a feature: convert it to numbers.
gd_e_ad_warn_const: Warning: these columns have the same value in every row, so they carry no information.
gd_e_ad_warn_small: Warning: some classes are very small.
gd_f_ad_warn_small: Add more samples or merge tiny classes; otherwise SMOTE and cross-validation may fail.
gd_unusable:
- Raw APK files or other binaries: this tool does not extract features. Extract them with another tool first and save the result as CSV.
- Text-only or image data with no numeric feature columns.
- Datasets without a label column (unlabelled data cannot train or evaluate a classifier).
- A label that is a continuous number (a regression target) or an identifier with many different values.
- A dataset where every sample has the same label.
- Excel (.xlsx), JSON or other formats: convert them to CSV.
- Several labels written in one cell, for example Adware;Banking. Each distinct text is treated as its own class.
